questions.q: According to this lesson, what are the two categories a Microsoft-stack BI developer interview mixes together?
options: Conceptual questions (design tradeoffs) and tool-specific questions (actually operating a feature)
Salary questions and scheduling questions
Questions about SQL Server only and questions about Power BI only
Behavioral questions and personality questions
questions.explain: Conceptual questions test whether you understand the reasoning behind a design choice; tool-specific questions test whether you've actually operated the tool that implements it.

questions.q: What's the key difference between a Type 1 and a Type 2 slowly changing dimension?
options: Type 1 overwrites history; Type 2 preserves it by adding new rows
Type 1 is used only in Power BI; Type 2 is used only in SSIS
Type 1 requires a snowflake schema; Type 2 requires a star schema
There is no meaningful difference between the two
questions.explain: A Type 1 SCD overwrites the old value with no history kept. A Type 2 SCD adds a new row so both the old and new values remain traceable over time.

questions.q: In Power BI, what is the key difference between a calculated column and a measure?
options: A calculated column is computed row-by-row and stored; a measure is computed at query time based on filter context
A calculated column can only hold text; a measure can only hold numbers
Measures are only available in the free version of Power BI
Calculated columns and measures are the exact same feature with different names
questions.explain: This distinction matters because it changes when and how the value is calculated — stored per row versus dynamically per query context.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend answering a tool-specific interview question by referencing your own capstone project?
options: Because it gives your answer something real and specific to point to, instead of a generic description remembered from a video
Because interviewers always ask to see your GitHub profile mid-question
Because tool-specific questions can only be answered using AdventureWorks data
Because generic answers are technically against most companies' interview policies
questions.explain: You didn't just read about a Lookup transformation or a DAX measure — you built one. Pointing to the real thing you built is stronger than reciting a remembered definition.

questions.q: What does DAX's CALCULATE function primarily manipulate, and why does that matter for interview prep?
options: Filter context — nearly every non-trivial DAX measure depends on understanding it
The physical storage location of a Power BI file
The formatting of numbers displayed on a report
The refresh schedule of a Power BI dataset
questions.explain: CALCULATE changes the filter context a DAX expression is evaluated within — a concept central to almost every real measure, which is why interviewers ask about it so often.
